analysis: The closest is a substantial communication programme: rhetorical theory and practice, persuasion, linguistic meaning, media history and forms, leadership/organisation/marketing, negotiation, audience research and qualitative/quantitative inquiry. It specifically responds to the target’s communication substance despite stated HCI, specialist research and thesis gaps. Replaced broad introductory economics with programming, which addresses an actual required computational foundation rather than only general market context.

The social-impact programme retains rhetorical, textual and media inquiry and materially changes the subject-matter priorities to climate, health, public representation, movements, justice and civil society. Climate and epidemiological foundations supply evidence for evaluating public messages, not substitutes for communication theory. Social theory explains identity, public spheres and organised collective claims. These are specific complementary roles rather than generic breadth.

The human/digital programme is reconstructed away from general rational-agent optimisation and Bayesian decision mathematics toward film/media meaning and higher cognitive functions, while retaining programming, mathematics, data, vision and neural methods with psycholinguistics and philosophy of mind. Courses provide a coherent academic response to human communication with digital tools, not an HCI or UX equivalence. Poetry/performance is creative communicative practice, not an app-design laboratory. The three substitutions follow specific source-backed concepts and all pairwise course changes materially alter priorities.

All 41 active courses were read from current profiles or available official descriptions. Description-only Market Research, Strategy and Digital Transformation, social movements, climate communication and psycholinguistics receive full consideration within their actual statements. Customer research is not embellished with unsupported named methods; psycholinguistics is human-language processing rather than automated NLP. Media Archaeology is material/cultural media history, From T.V. to TikTok is American social history and representation, and Creative Communication Laboratory is poetic/artistic practice. None is mislabelled generic digital product design.

Three original offering conflicts are resolved. The closest no longer schedules introductory economics outside its only planned first term. Psycholinguistics is moved to its only planned Spring-2027 slot after Brain and Behaviour. Vision follows programming in Spring-2029. Higher cognitive functions follows the brain foundation; ML follows data workflows and precedes deep learning. The social-impact option places foundational sociology before modern theory and civil-society inquiry and methods before behavioural analysis. Formal prerequisites, covered offerings, twenty-four unique courses/four per term, first-year PPD and six advanced courses all pass.

Fourteen partial placements and twelve meaningful gaps cover all external subjects and UCR courses once. Corrected old style-to-quantitative-content-analysis, social-media-to-HCI and international-business-to-responsible-strategic-communication relationships; they were based on overly broad common labels. Philosophy matches now specify thinking/technology and AI ethics, not generic analytical transfer. Statistics is placed with actual behavioural statistical modelling, academic English with the bounded academic writing function, and the separate experiment remains a gap. Optional research remains outside the scheduled 180 EC, in parallel with the individual thesis.

alignment.rationale: Both develop research-based academic writing, structured argument, source use and presentation. Tilburg specifically teaches English register, grammar and mechanics; UCR combines these academic-writing functions with personal development and civic engagement.
Both develop brands, marketing communication and consumer engagement using audience evidence and responsible strategy. The selected tools and project contexts differ.

Both teach measurement, research design, surveys, experiments, reliability, validity and ethics. UCR additionally conducts an empirical team project; Tilburg applies the framework specifically to communication research.

Both investigate communication within groups and organisations. UCR centres leadership communication, ethical influence and a leader’s communication challenge; Tilburg teaches wider collaboration and organisational-communication theory.

Both address employee motivation, teams, leadership, power, culture and organisational change. UCR provides organisational-psychology evidence; Tilburg specifically investigates communication channels, employee voice and an internal communication audit.

Both examine ethical and social questions about AI, autonomy and human interaction. Tilburg centres media society, public space, ideology and algorithmic bias; UCR combines AI ethics with psychological, organisational and care relationships.

Both introduce Python, variables, loops, functions, data formats and debugging. UCR also develops recursion and object-oriented programming; Tilburg emphasises communication-related text and data applications.

Both examine the nature of thinking and effects of technology on minds through philosophical arguments. Tilburg additionally covers philosophy of science and ethics; UCR centres mind, consciousness and experience.
Both design, conduct and report human-subject research through interviews. UCR emphasises qualitative methods and interpretation, while Tilburg also carries out and analyses survey research.

Both investigate cognition such as attention, memory, emotion and control using empirical studies. UCR centres neural mechanisms and a cognitive experiment; Tilburg connects cognitive findings more broadly to communication.

Both select, conduct and interpret statistical analyses of human data, including group comparisons and relationships, and report results. UCR adds experimental-design and multivariable modelling; Tilburg teaches the introductory communication-statistics workflow.

Both analyse communication through theoretical models, including rhetoric and influence. UCR concentrates on classical rhetoric, argument and public speech; Tilburg also covers interpersonal relations, media effects and active audiences.

Both apply communication knowledge to a real social challenge with an external partner. UCR centres rhetorical education and public speaking with local schoolchildren; Tilburg develops a communication strategy and conceptual plan.

Both study persuasive strategies, attitudes and behaviour and apply them to messages for a specific audience. UCR develops community communication about sustainable lifestyles; Tilburg surveys persuasion theories and message design.
Media, cognition, AI ethics and computing provide related foundations, but none of the selected courses centres usability, UX and the design and evaluation of human-technology interaction.
No selected UCR course supplies dedicated Dutch academic-language instruction.
Several courses teach design and analysis or conduct research, but none is counted again as this separate full-cycle communication experiment.
Stylistics and data workflows contribute related tools, but no selected course centres quantitative language-corpus collection, reliable manual and automatic annotation and content analysis.

Organisational psychology, persuasion and business governance contribute related perspectives, but no selected course provides the dedicated stakeholder, reputation, crisis and strategic-communication sequence.
AI ethics, programming, neural models and organisational transformation supply separate foundations, not a dedicated course on generative conversational technology in organisational communication.
The selected Content Marketing and Analytics elective joins content strategy and audience-oriented data analysis. No selected UCR course supplies that combined specialism.
Thirty credits remain open for approved exchange study; no host or course package is invented.
Persuasion and psychology supply relevant concepts, but no selected UCR course centres iterative persuasive interaction design and evaluation using user data.
Creative practice and cognitive science contribute in different courses, but none is counted again as the dedicated psychology-of-creativity elective.
Social theory, media analysis and ethics inform public debate, but no selected course supplies this dedicated misinformation and polarisation elective.
The individual communication-science systematic literature-review thesis remains a separate requirement. Optional UCR independent research is additional to the scheduled 180 credits.
